title: Cleaning One Tape
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, choose its initial state $q_0$, a Boolean input $x$, a tape index $i<k$, an input-head position, an output word, an integer bound $B$, integer endpoints $a\le b$, and tape contents $D_t,M_t$ with head positions $D_p$. Suppose $a\le0\le b$, $-B\le a-1$, $b+1\le B$, and $a\le D_p(i)\le b$. Suppose that writing false at the scanned cell of the $i$th tape of $M_t$ when it does not already contain true, and otherwise leaving it unchanged, produces the tape that has true at the origin, false on the interval from $a$ to $b$, and blank elsewhere. Also suppose the nonblank cells of $D_t(i)$ lie in $[a,b]$, and every head position in $D_p$ has absolute value at most $B$. Then the cleaning machine, started in the cleaning phase for tape $i$ at its marking stage with these tapes and positions, reaches some time $T$ by which every work-tape head position at every time $t\le T$ has absolute value at most $B$, and its configuration at time $T$ has the next cleaning state, unchanged input-head position and output, and both tape families blank with all their heads at zero except that the stated tape index advances according to the cleaning successor.
hypotheses_covered: machine M with k Boolean work tapes, initial state q₀, and state type S
Boolean input x; tape index i<k; input-head position and output word
integer bound B and endpoints a,b
specified write-or-leave-unchanged transformation of M_t(i) equals the marked interval tape
nonblank support of D_t(i) lies in [a,b]
every head position D_p(j) has absolute value at most B
caveat: The conclusion is stated via the defined cleaning successor; the formal equality also updates the two tape families and both head-position families at index i.
